svg.text: Laws, enforcement and fatal-crash data for 50 states + DC
Who is behind the wheel, where a DUI becomes a felony, and what tools states use.
Prior DWI convictions among impaired drivers in fatal crashes
FARS 2024, drivers with known history; impaired = driver-impairment code 9
of impaired drivers in fatal crashes had
no prior DWI conviction on record
5,360 impaired drivers with known history, 403 with a prior
No prior conviction on record is not the same as never having driven impaired.
Mississippi: 0 of 49 impaired drivers show a prior; likely a reporting gap, still counted.
Number of DUI convictions that makes a DUI a felony
One tile per jurisdiction (50 states + DC), grouped by threshold
Sobriety checkpoints and mandatory vehicle impound
Checkpoints = legal in the state. Impound = mandatory seizure on a DUI. Segment width = number of jurisdictions.
Neither tool: AK, ID, MT, TX, WY
Killed drivers with a known BAC result, by testing law
Each dot is one jurisdiction. Tick = simple average of jurisdictions (not weighted by drivers).
Share of killed drivers with a known BAC result. Lowest MS 9.6%, highest VT 97.7%.
Alcohol-impaired deaths per 100 million vehicle miles
Five highest and five lowest of 51 jurisdictions. NHTSA imputed BAC 0.08+, 2024 deaths; FHWA 2022 miles.
Data from public sources: NHTSA FARS 2024, NASID, NCSL, FHWA, state statutes
Laws as compiled in 2026. FARS counts convictions on record, not impairment history; per-mile rates use 2022 FHWA miles.
